summary: Bossangoa Airport (BSN/FEFS) is a small regional airport serving the town of Bossangoa in the Ouham Prefecture of north-central Central African Republic. It primarily supports humanitarian, missionary, and light charter operations, as the region has limited road infrastructure. The facility provides vital air access for one of the more remote populated areas of the country.
faqs:
Q: Does Bossangoa Airport have scheduled commercial flights?
A: No scheduled commercial service operates at this airport; flights are typically charter, humanitarian, or missionary in nature.

Q: What is the runway surface like at Bossangoa Airport?
A: The airport has an unpaved or minimally developed runway suitable primarily for small propeller aircraft.

Q: Are there customs and immigration facilities?
A: No permanent customs or immigration facilities are available; advance arrangements are required for international arrivals.

Q: Is the airport operational year-round?
A: Operations can be affected by seasonal weather and regional security conditions, so travelers should confirm status in advance.
transport_tips: Ground transport from the airport to Bossangoa town center is typically by 4x4 vehicle or motorcycle taxi due to road conditions. There is no public transit serving the airport, so arranging private transport in advance is strongly recommended. Travelers flying in should coordinate pickup directly with their host organization or charter operator.
local_tip: Coordinate all logistics through a local contact or NGO before arrival, as there are no on-site services and the surrounding road network becomes very difficult to navigate during the rainy season from May to October.
